{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMdNDs8AAAABahnSqw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnXy5zhEIF7s", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnXy5", "number": 52, "title": "Use the licensed Uka PMX model for representative converter and demo tests", "body": "## Problem

The current **Synthetic rigs** demo and the large Playwright matrix primarily exercise box/wedge fixtures. These are valuable for independent numerical oracles and edge cases, but are hard to understand visually and are not representative of a feature-rich MMD character. The full browser CI also took about **77 minutes** in [run #66](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/actions/runs/40159817349) (79 tests, one worker), with extensive repeated screenshots.

We should use a real, clearly licensed MMD character as the primary **human-readable integration example**, instead of treating the synthetic box/wedge models as the central visual testing experience.

## Chosen asset: CG-CA Uka

Use **Uka**, not a newly authored model:

- Upstream: https://github.com/mmdagent-ex/uka
- PMX: https://github.com/mmdagent-ex/uka/blob/main/MS_Uka.pmx (4,217,254 bytes in the currently inspected upstream tree)
- Textures: https://github.com/mmdagent-ex/uka/tree/main/tex
- Example VMD files: https://github.com/mmdagent-ex/uka/tree/main/motion
- Original Japanese rights notice: https://github.com/mmdagent-ex/uka/blob/main/README.ja.md
- Upstream documents **CC BY 4.0** for files in its repository, including an explicit attribution string and additional usage guidelines. **This is not CC0**. Preserve the full notice/guidelines, credit, source link and change information. Do not imply endorsement or unrestricted uses contrary to upstream terms.
- Upstream states approximately 49,951 vertices, 77,907 faces, 10 materials, 301 bones, 148 morphs, 164 rigid bodies and 151 joints. Those counts describe the *source asset*, not guaranteed current converter support.
- Original credit (verbatim): `CG-CA Uka (c) 2023-2024 by Nagoya Institute of Technology, Moonshot R&D Goal 1 Avatar Symbiotic Society`.

## Expected outcome

The normal demo and representative end-to-end regression tests use **the real Uka PMX as input to this repository's converter**, with an actual converter-produced glTF/GLB rendered through the existing plugins. A developer or visitor should be able to see what is being tested: a recognizable character, with clear feature demonstrations and stated limitations.

Keep purpose-built synthetic fixtures **where their known scalar/GPU oracle or unusual boundary inputs are needed**. Do not delete or weaken meaningful conformance checks merely to make Uka the main example.

## Implementation requirements

1. **Rights and reproducible acquisition.** Review both upstream READMEs and guidelines against public demo, CI, caching and any redistribution. Pin an upstream commit and exact **SHA-256/size** for the allowlisted PMX, required textures, selected VMD files and notices. Prefer the existing Gene-style fetch/cache/verify workflow; avoid committing large third-party binary assets. Download only required files. Do not silently substitute missing files. Supply a provenance/attribution and derivative-use record in docs and generated output.
2. **Inventory the actual source model before choosing conversion options.** Parse Uka and record the real vertex skinning types, material/texture references, supported and unsupported morph types, IK/append/grants, physics bodies/joints, and the selected VMD contents. Confirm which bounded converter/runtime modes are actually usable. Do **not** claim SDEF/QDEF/physics/animation support for this particular PMX without checking. If unsupported records prevent full conversion, retain an honest, useful **supported subset** and explicit warnings; don't silently approximate or invent support.
3. **Convert Uka through the normal pipeline** into reproducible glTF/GLB artifacts for the demo/tests; verify asset resolution, glTF Validator core errors, loader/plugin registration, and browser rendering. Avoid writing a model-specific converter shortcut or modifying the general conversion contract just to pass Uka.
4. **Make Uka a first-class, legible example** in the unified demo. Prefer the same clear original-PMX versus converted-GLB comparison where practical, with comparable view/camera/lighting and simple controls to inspect Toon/PBR, Outline and supported deformation/motions. For unsupported features, give specific, visible limitations rather than presenting a control that does nothing. Preserve the Gene Light comparison if it provides distinct useful coverage. The synthetic test rigs should not be the default end-user demonstration.
5. **Rework representative browser coverage around Uka**: verify real asset loading/conversion and visible rendering, material/Outline differences, and at least one meaningful supported pose/motion/deformation scenario if the audited converter profile permits it. Document exactly which Uka features are and are not exercised.
6. **Reduce redundant full-browser tests.** Audit the repeated synthetic rig/motion/format screenshot matrix: use Uka for representative visual integration scenarios, retain minimal synthetic cases for independent pixel/vertex oracle, and move cheap parsing/edge-case checks to Node tests. Keep necessary regression coverage and failure diagnostics. Measure and report full browser CI duration against run #66's ~77-minute browser baseline. Do not merely increase timeouts or add parallel jobs as a substitute for examining redundant work.
7. **Practicality.** Uka's upstream texture directory is roughly 85 MB, so document the impact on checkout/build/Pages and use an explicit asset allowlist, with no unnecessary asset duplication. Keep generated files reproducible and the build workable in the existing public GitHub Actions setup; do not assume paid runners.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] A pinned and rights-reviewed Uka source manifest, attribution and original notice/guideline links are checked in; only intentionally selected source files are fetched, checksum verified and converted.
- [ ] A documented Uka feature inventory distinguishes actual source content, currently supported conversion paths, skipped/unsupported functions and any approximation. Conversion does not silently discard significant unsupported behavior.
- [ ] Demo displays Uka converted via the normal PMX→glTF pipeline and gives a clear way to compare it to source-PMX rendering where supported. A user can tell which observable feature is being demonstrated.
- [ ] Real Uka browser integration checks pass for meaningful supported functionality; synthetic numerical/conformance oracles and malformed-input boundary tests remain sound. CI evidence demonstrates no unintentional coverage loss.
- [ ] Image captures are selective, diagnostic on failure and not multiplied across the entire Cartesian product without justification. Report before/after full browser duration, test counts, removed/replaced checks and retained coverage; explain any remaining large runtime.
- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run check:links` and `git diff --check` pass in the PR CI; any unsupported optional WebGPU checks are clearly labeled.
- [ ] No unsupported MMD-fidelity claim is made: Three.js PMX reference rendering is not the original MikuMikuDance renderer.

## Optional validation

Compare Uka's original-PMX and generated-glTF screenshots at a fixed camera for a representative pose, and add a short visual validation record. Do not require an original-MMD executable for this task.

## Required post-merge verification

After the merge-triggered Pages deployment, check that the public demo successfully loads Uka and its allowed textures, that the selected views/controls work without console/network errors, and that the deployment workflow succeeded. Record the deployed result.

## Out of scope

Inventing a new model, implementing every unsupported MMD feature, asserting original MMD visual/physical fidelity, introducing a new CI platform or paid runners, or deleting all synthetic fixtures.
